The 3 Scientific Breakthroughs Explained

Breakthrough 1: Data Hygiene

Power-Law Variance De-skewing (log1p)

Feature skewness in raw Ethereum logs reached an astounding 99.19 (for transaction values). Applying np.log1p stabilized the heavy tail and prevented 99% of normal transactions from being crushed into zero. This alone propelled centralized F1 from 70.39% to 88.22%.

Breakthrough 2: Architecture

Eliminating Non-IID BatchNorm Corruption

Batch Normalization relies on local running mean & variance. Under extreme Dirichlet skew (α=0.01), clients hold disjoint label distributions; averaging their BN layers mathematically corrupts the global model. Removing BatchNorm lifted Federated ROC-AUC from 0.7349 to 0.9779!

Breakthrough 3: Aggregation

Vanilla SGD Fixed-Step Regularization

Local momentum buffers pull weights into conflicting directions across communication rounds. Replacing adaptive local momentum with pure, unaccelerated SGD updates acts as a natural regularizer, ensuring steady convergence across 50 communication rounds.

The Blockchain Fraud Detection Trilemma

Decentralized blockchain ledgers (such as Ethereum) provide transparency and pseudonymity, which malicious actors exploit for phishing scams, automated money-laundering bots, and fake token contracts. Traditional Machine Learning relies on centralizing logs, which creates single points of failure and violates privacy laws. This research implements a 5-stage framework solving the three fundamental bottlenecks:

1. Data Privacy & GDPR

Decentralized wallets and exchanges cannot pool raw client transaction logs. Federated Learning keeps raw data strictly local on client nodes.

2. Non-IID Statistical Drift

Retail wallets vs institutional exchanges hold radically skewed transaction distributions. SGD with momentum provides fixed-step regularization against drift.

3. Black-Box Opacity

Regulators demand human-interpretable justifications. Post-hoc central SHAP and LIME deliver audit trails with zero client communication overhead.

System Architecture Diagram

Stage 1: Preprocessing, Data Hygiene & Feature Selection

Raw blockchain logs are plagued by high-dimensional noise, administrative identifiers, zero-variance columns, and missing values. The preprocessing pipeline applies strict data hygiene to avoid data leakage and isolate the 20 most predictive tabular features.

1. Dropping Identifiers

Removed ['Unnamed: 0', 'Index', 'Address']. Hexadecimal wallet addresses memorize past entities and cause catastrophic data leakage.

2. Zero-Variance Columns

Identified and stripped 7 columns containing constant values across all 9,841 accounts (e.g., ERC20 avg time between sent tnx).

3. Rigorous Imputation

Continuous numerical features imputed with Mean. Categorical features imputed with Mode, followed by category encoding.

Dataset Class Distribution (FLAG)

Normal Accounts: 7,662 (77.86%) | Loss Weight = 0.642 Fraud Accounts: 2,179 (22.14%) | Loss Weight = 2.258

Stage 2: Decentralized Client Simulation (Dirichlet Non-IID Skew)

In decentralized systems, transaction volumes and fraud ratios vary wildly between entities. To model this, the paper partitions training data across 20 simulated edge nodes using a Dirichlet Distribution parameterized by concentration α:

p(x1, ..., xk; α) = (1 / B(α)) ∏ xiαi - 1

Experimental Client Partition Plot (α = 0.01)

Stage 5: Post-Hoc Explainable AI (XAI) Framework

A core innovation of this paper is Zero Communication Overhead: Rather than forcing resource-constrained edge client nodes to compute costly Shapley values, explainability is executed centrally on the aggregated global model post-training.

#1 Top Indicator
ERC20 Uniq Rec Token Name

Diversity in received custom token names. Phishing scam contracts send automated airdrops using novel token labels.

#2 Top Indicator
Total Ether Balance

Near-zero or volatile balances. Malicious accounts act as disposable "mules", sweeping stolen ether instantly.

#3 Top Indicator
Avg Min Between Received Tnx

Extremely low temporal intervals reflect automated bot activity rather than human transaction pacing.

#4 Top Indicator
ERC20 Max & Avg Val Sent

Sudden anomalous monetary spikes that deviate sharply from the account's historical median.

1. FedProx Regularization Sweep (μ ∈ [0.0, 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05]) α=0.01 Skew

Higher proximal penalties (μ=0.05) anchor local updates to the global model, preventing client drift and elevating F1 to 47.24% and ROC-AUC to 0.9240.

2. Personalized FL (FedPer): Local Utility vs Global Generalization Split Architecture

Private local classification heads achieve 66.67% F1 locally, proving ideal for edge nodes, but suffer positive bias when ensembled across out-of-distribution global test sets.

3. Rescuing Tabular Self-Attention from Non-IID Collapse LayerNorm + FedProx

Hasan et al. reported Transformer collapse to 72.88%. Our pre-LayerNorm MultiHead Attention with FedProx eliminates wild gradient oscillations, stabilizing accuracy at 82.28%.

4. Novel Discovery: Client-Aware SHAP Feature Attribution Drift Multi-Client Audit

Auditing 3 client archetypes reveals feature drift: Retail wallets rely on Time Longevity (SHAP: 0.1008), while malicious clusters trigger on ERC20 min val rec (SHAP: 0.1316).

⚠️ Scientific Casualties & Theoretical Trade-Offs (Defense Discussion Points)

1. The Personalization vs. Generalization Trade-Off:

In EXP-08 (FedPer), keeping local heads private yielded 66.67% local F1, but ensembling them on the global test set resulted in false-positive bias. Under α=0.01, fraud-dominant nodes drift to high positive biases, making global ensembling conservative.

2. Attention Weight Divergence in FedAvg:

In EXP-09, Multi-Head Self-Attention oscillated violently between predicting 100% normal and 100% fraud across communication rounds. Applying FedProx proximal anchoring (μ=0.05) in EXP-10 eliminated this oscillation by penalizing local attention head drift.
